Its Python2 syntax and integer-division assumptions are historical; a forget-gate comment conflicts with the positive bias assigned, so inspect code rather than inherit the comment. The NES gist shows a fixed-variance Gaussian population, standardized rewards and a noise-weighted parameter update against a known toy target; printed convergence is a captured example, not a rerun. The Torch fast-LSTM gist explicitly credits Justin Johnson for optimization and batches gate matrix operations; do not count it as an independent Karpathy invention. MicroGPT contains dependency-free scalar autograd, character tokenization, a one-layer cached causal transformer, stable softmax, RMS normalization, Adam and generation in one file; its names dataset and educational scale do not demonstrate production quality or human identity knowledge. The CSS gist changes historical Google Slides speaker-note geometry; it has no broad engineering-rule evidence.

This batch contains package manifests, ignore rules, licenses and build settings, not new personal philosophies. MIT notices preserve attribution and warranty terms without proving per-line authorship. Ignore files separate datasets, runtime caches, artifacts and secrets from tracked code; autoresearch additionally excludes generated per-session agent prompt files and results. Requirements range from historical pins to unconstrained dependencies; no current compatibility or security is certified. Autoresearch pins a CUDA-specific Torch index and Python>=3.10, while several newer utilities use uv project manifests and .env exclusions. MatlabWrapper and EigenLibSVM build files explicitly encode local include/link paths and tiny demo targets, supporting the need to establish a working local environment rather than assume copied paths. Micrograd packaging declares its scalar educational scope; minGPT setup depends on Torch. Council frontend manifest is a React/Vite template configuration. These operational sources are preserved individually but not inflated into dozens of independent behavioral examples.

Arxiv-sanity-lite intake batches 100 papers, preserves newest versions by timestamp, stops after unchanged batches to spare the API, and signals whether feature recomputation is needed. Inspection finds the retry counter advances on exceptions but not on short successful pages, so a short page can loop indefinitely; this was not reproduced. API parsing normalizes feed records and version IDs but assumes expected fields. Database helpers centralize paths and distinguish read-only/write-open modes; a StackOverflow-credited temporary-write/rename pattern protects pickle readers, with historical platform portability not certified. Compressed pickle storage assumes trusted local data. Feature computation fits TF-IDF on a possible subset then transforms all title/abstract/author text, stores float32 vectors and ID mappings. The Makefile is a convenience launcher, not an independently verified production scheduler.

Server status, prices and credential-storage examples are historical, not current recommended secret handling. The calorie README describes a deliberately simple two-counter self-tracking app with editable assumed metabolic rate and deficit; it is a personal utility description, not verified medical or nutrition guidance.

The email recommender trains a balanced LinearSVC for each nonempty user tag, restricts suggestions to recent untagged papers, merges candidates by maximum tag score and renders a bounded HTML list. It skips missing email, insufficient tagged examples and empty recommendation sets. A dry-run option prevents the send call, but the send helper merely prints status and does not establish delivery, while the final sent counter also increments on dry runs. This is source inspection, not authorization to send email or a verified production delivery mechanism. Historical SendGrid file-key conventions are not adopted into AI OS.

Arxiv-sanity-lite backend exposes random/time/text/tag/exemplar ranking, pagination, inspection of TF-IDF and SVM weights, and user-tag/email preferences through lazy per-request database handles. Inspection makes feature contributions visible rather than hiding ranking behind a score. The source uses username-only sessions and a fallback dev signing key, GET mutations and limited old email validation; this is a historical prototype, not a hardened authentication model to adopt. React paper/detail/tag components render scores and links and send prompt-driven add/remove requests, but report responses only to console without refreshing state or explicit error UI. This code was read, not deployed or interacted with.

The arxiv-sanity-lite frontend exposes explicit ranking filters, tag shortcuts, paper feature weights, date-window statistics and responsive presentation. Its profile is deliberately username-only and warns email delivery may fail; this is a historical prototype rather than hardened authentication. The thumbnail daemon skips cached outputs and limits download and converter time, logging failures and terminating stuck conversion. Templates load external React and Babel, and some UI handling logs errors rather than displaying them. These files describe interface and reliability choices, not personal beliefs; no network or subprocess behavior was executed.

The preserver pipeline fetches versioned arXiv records incrementally with an explicit gentle wait and a stated early-stop assumption. PDFs are cached with timeouts; failed PDF conversion creates an empty marker, so attempted acquisition is not successful extraction. Analyze filters suspicious text lengths, fits TF-IDF on a seeded subset for memory efficiency, transforms the complete retained corpus and precomputes nearest neighbors. Buildsvm balances positive libraries against other papers. Make_cache precomputes dates, popularity and weighted lexical search to speed startup; its comments acknowledge missing bigram search. SQL defines user and library tables and contains destructive initialization statements that were read but never executed. Historical cache correctness, platform portability and completeness were not verified.

The preserver pipeline fetches versioned arXiv records incrementally with an explicit gentle wait and a stated early-stop assumption. Analyze filters suspicious text lengths, fits TF-IDF on a seeded subset for memory efficiency, transforms the complete retained corpus and precomputes nearest neighbors. The preserver server offers lexical search, nearest-neighbor paper lookup with stale-version fallback, personalized SVM recommendations excluding saved papers, popularity, social libraries and discussion tags. These are historical implementation details read in full, not deployable guarantees or universal persona rules.

The explicitly BSD-attributed Karpathy canvas engine abstracts update/draw/init and mouse/keyboard callbacks so educational demos can focus on learning behavior. Toy geometry and reward shaping do not prove general-purpose performance; regression neuron plotting uses grid-count as neuron count and may read undefined values. Pooling saves winner coordinates for gradient routing and possible visualization; its finite -99999 initial maximum is a stated assumption. These mathematical mechanisms and uncertainty boundaries were fully read, not reproduced.

Unsupported configuration logs can leave incomplete setups. These are source implementation observations, not runtime certification.

Trainer accumulates gradients until batch boundaries, adds L1 and L2 terms and implements SGD momentum, Adagrad, moving-window gradients, Adadelta, Nesterov and Adam. Adam bias corrections multiply rather than divide by one-minus-beta-power; this historical implementation must not be treated as a current correct reference. Utilities provide cached Box-Muller Gaussian sampling, typed-array zeros, permutations and weighted sampling with assumed normalized probabilities. Vol holds weights and gradients, initializes variance proportional to inverse fan-in and deliberately serializes weights but not gradients. Augmentation square-crops with zero-padding outside bounds and flips; grayscale takes the red channel rather than luminance and image conversion aborts selected browser errors. Jasmine boot is vendored third-party test framework initialization and contributes no Karpathy persona claim. Full source read, no execution.

Historical Covid-sanity Twitter daemon warm-starts collected tweets, searches paper v1 URLs excluding replies and retweets, filters banned accounts and preserves full text and author metrics. It explicitly calls the assumed v1 URL sketchy and slightly wrong. It writes a temporary JSON then renames it, preserves old results on broad API exceptions, and revisits recent hundred papers between older chunks while sleeping for a historical rate limit. The server must restart to reload results. This is architectural evidence for recency-prioritized incremental collection, not a verified current X API collector; broad exception handling and platform rename semantics remain limitations. No credentials read and no API executed.

Cryptos implements Bitcoin secp256k1 constants and transparent educational primitives: finite-field point addition, double-and-add scalar multiplication, public-key compression, hash160 and Base58Check addresses, DER signature encoding, double-SHA256 ECDSA and eighty-byte block headers. Curves credit Wikipedia for extended Euclid; modular inverse does not check coprimality and point operations do not validate curve membership. ECDSA explicitly leaves deterministic nonce and constant-time protection as TODOs; validation is basic, uses raw x rather than explicit modulo-n reduction and is not production cryptography. Block validation only tests proof-of-work, with target-field validation TODO; retarget caps elapsed interval and maximum target. Empty package initializer has no semantic content. Keys use OS randomness with rejection sampling and address checksum validation. Full read without running cryptographic or financial actions.

ECDSA explicitly leaves deterministic nonce and constant-time protection as TODOs; validation is basic, uses raw x rather than explicit modulo-n reduction and is not production cryptography. Block validation only tests proof-of-work, with target-field validation TODO; retarget caps elapsed interval and maximum target. Empty package initializer has no semantic content. Keys use OS randomness with rejection sampling and address checksum validation. Full read without running cryptographic or financial actions.

Cryptos network decomposes Bitcoin wire messages into dataclass payloads and a checksum-validated envelope, explicitly serializes endian conventions, assumes IPv4 and supports version/verack, ping/pong and header requests. Header decoder asserts zero transactions; the baby node automatically acknowledges versions and responds to pings. Version decoding remains a fixed default TODO stub, handshake advertises zero timestamp and nonce with a programmingbitcoin user agent, and getheaders encoder only supplies one locator despite a configurable count. Socket operations lack timeout and payload size validation is permissive. These transparent educational protocol pieces support mechanism-first instruction; they are not a complete production peer or verified live network integration. Full source read, no network connection.

SHA256 follows named FIPS sections from bit operations through prime-root constants, message padding, sixty-four-word schedule, compression rounds and digest accumulation; it explicitly says this is purely educational and should not serve serious use. Constants are regenerated via floating-point roots each call, a performance and precision boundary rather than production optimization. RIPEMD160 explicitly reuses and cleans up an existing implementation credited to Bjorn Edstrom and Markus Friedl; its bytes-to-bytes wrapper, buffered block processing, parallel eighty-round branches and final state combination are fully read, with a little-endian-only assertion. Reuse is credited rather than falsely treating all cryptographic mechanisms as Karpathy original thinking. No cryptographic correctness tests executed.

Cryptos tests compare SHA256 with hashlib, RIPEMD with credited known vectors, Bitcoin addresses and SEC encodings with Mastering Bitcoin and Programming Bitcoin fixtures, wire-message round trips, legacy and SegWit parsing, fees, coinbase classification and height. Transaction tests deliberately tamper signatures and keys then restore them to show verification failure and recovery. Some tests require network lookup or live handshake and were not executed. Deep-vector-quantization empty initializers contain no information; CIFAR module uses randomized training crops/flips versus tensor-only validation, shuffled/drop-last pinned batches and reuses validation for test. Encoder/decoder explicitly credit DeepMind Sonnet VQVAE architecture. Loss module leaves logit-Laplace unimplemented and notes a tentative DeepMind factor-of-two discrepancy in normal reconstruction loss, so metric comparisons require normalizer awareness rather than assuming identical scales. Full text read, attribution retained.

OpenAI encoder/decoder explicitly adapts official DALL-E code: moves boundary one-by-one convolutions into quantization for cleaner symmetric comparisons and removes precision/device machinery to keep things simple; shape, channel and float32 checks remain. Quantize contrasts nearest-codebook VQVAE with Gumbel categorical relaxation, straight-through gradients, commitment/embedding losses and KL-to-uniform. VQVAE adds empirically needed data-driven kmeans initialization with an explicit multi-GPU TODO. Full Lightning model separates encoder, discrete bottleneck and decoder, logs reconstruction plus cluster perplexity/use to diagnose collapse, and asserts optimizer decay partition is disjoint and complete. Schedules credit DALL-E but openly approximate incompatible KL normalization with an empirically working scale; logit-Laplace choice remains unavailable. Seeded training and best validation reconstruction checkpoint are specified, not executed. Comparisons preserve upstream attribution and empirical uncertainty.

EigenLibSVM Karpathy-authored 2012 wrappers translate dense Eigen rows into LibSVM nodes, validate data/label dimensions and parameters, expose linear weights, C and model persistence, and explicitly warn about imbalance and missing cross-validation. Test prints expected MATLAB margins and approximately 0.945 training accuracy before and after save/load, rather than claiming held-out evaluation. Prediction allocates D nodes without the required terminating sentinel; source is historical and not correctness-certified. Matrix serialization helper credits Alex Teichman and notes newline-dependent ASCII parsing, so it is third-party evidence. Find-birds separates bounded depth-one acquisition with disk pickle caching and manual Tweepy error waits from offline recommendation: mutual-follow counts discounted by logarithmic popularity, expensive formatting only after top-list selection, then a plain HTML report. Incomplete cached users are explicitly skipped; remote descriptions inserted without escaping are a rendering limitation. These scripts were read without executing credentials, network collection or pickle payloads.

Training begins with UTF-8 bytes, counts adjacent pairs and repeatedly replaces the most frequent pair with a new token. Encoding follows the lowest learned merge rank and stops when no available pair exists. Decoding concatenates vocabulary bytes and uses replacement on invalid UTF-8. Regex boundaries and special tokens are explicitly excluded. The training loop assumes a remaining pair exists; no tiny-input safeguard is explicit in this source.

Training counts pairs only within regex-defined chunks, preserving category boundaries. Ordinary encoding processes chunks independently. Special-token registration stores forward and inverse maps. Encoding explicitly chooses all, none, none_raise or a permitted set; the default asserts that registered special strings are absent. Allowed special strings are escaped before regex splitting, then encoded separately. Invalid token IDs raise ValueError; UTF-8 decoding uses replacement. The absence check is implemented as an assertion, so this educational code should not be certified as a hardened input boundary under optimized Python. Historical GPT pattern labels are source labels, not a verified current API contract.

Neuraltalk2 documents captioning, pretrained evaluation, data preprocessing, staged CNN finetuning and visualization, with explicit beam-search speed/quality tradeoffs and a known corrupt input-image failure. Its 2016 update recommends Google im2txt and preserves this as educational Torch code; projected leaderboard placement and speed are dated reports. semantic_note: nanochat unifies tokenizer, pretraining, midtraining, SFT, optional RL, inference and report card into a minimal baseline, with architectural choices initially based on single runs rather than exhaustive tuning. Recovery learning should not reward manufacturing errors; tokenizer regex replacement needs expert review and large tests.
